summary: Volker Caumanns is a Tibetologist who earned an MA at the University of Hamburg under David P. Jackson and a PhD at LMU Munich under Franz-Karl Ehrhard. He held posts at LMU Munich, Lumbini International Research Institute, and University of Bern.

Volker Grabowsky is a historian and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Kiel (~1978–1986). He held posts at the University of Passau, University of Hamburg, National University of Laos, and University of Münster (~1999–2007).
W. F. Jayasuriya worked in the field of Buddhist studies. He studied under teachers Rerukane Ariyaratne (attested 1963), H. D. Dharmasiriwardhana, and M. U. Sri Kaveeswara.
W. H. D. Rouse (1863–1950) was a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. He completed his education at Cheltenham College and Christ's College, Cambridge (~1882–1886).

W. H. R. Rivers (1864–1922) studied at Tonbridge School, Barts and The London School of Medicine and Dentistry, University of London, and St John's College, Cambridge. He held academic posts at University College London and the University of Cambridge.

W. Norman Brown (1892–1975) was an Indologist and historian. He studied at Hiram College and Johns Hopkins University, training under Maurice Bloomfield and Franklin Edgerton, and served as a professor at the University of Pennsylvania (attested 1969–1973).

W. Randolph Kloetzli earned a PhD at the University of Chicago (1964), studying under figures including Mircea Eliade, Paul Tillich, and J. A. B. van Buitenen. He lectured at American University, George Washington University, and Dartmouth College.

W. S. Karunaratne (1928–1986) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. Educated at Dharmaraja College, Ananda College, University of Ceylon, and SOAS University of London, he served as Dean of Oriental Studies at the University of Ceylon.

W. S. Karunatillake worked in linguistics, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He was a professor at the University of Kelaniya (attested 1997) and served as Visiting Numata Professor of Buddhist Studies at Harvard University in 1998.

Wai-lun Tam works in religious studies, sinology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at McMaster University under Koichi Shinohara and served as professor and department chair at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (attested 2016).

Walpola Rahula (1907–1997) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the universities of Calcutta, Ceylon (under G. P. Malalasekera), and Paris (under Paul Demiéville). He also held a post at the University of Oxford.

Walter Eugene Clark (1881–1960) was a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Harvard University (~1899–1906), he held academic posts at the University of Chicago (1923–1927) and Harvard University as Wales Professor of Sanskrit (1927–1950).
Walter Ewer (1784–1863) was an Indology and history scholar. He studied at Fort William College from ~1803 to 1805 and served in the Indian Civil Service from ~1803 to 1840.

Walter Liebenthal (1886–1982) was a scholar in Buddhist studies, sinology, and Indology. Over his career, he held academic appointments at the University of Paris, Visva-Bharati University (~1952–1959), and the University of Tübingen (~1960–1965).

Walter M. Spink (1928–2019) was a scholar of history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Amherst College (~1945–1949) and held academic posts at Brandeis University (~1956–1961) and the University of Michigan (attested 2005).

Walter Simon (1893–1981) was a scholar of sinology, Tibetology, and linguistics. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin under Otto Franke, later teaching there (1926, 1932–1934) and at SOAS, University of London (~1938–1960).

Walter Slaje (born 1954) is a scholar in the field of Indology. He completed his studies at the University of Vienna (~1978–1983) and served as a professor at the University of Halle-Wittenberg (~2000–2019).

Walter Yeeling Evans-Wentz (1878–1965) studied religious studies, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He was educated at Stanford University, the University of Oxford, and Jesus College, and later studied under the traditional teacher Kazi Dawa Samdup (~1919–1922).
Walther Schubring (1881–1969) was an Indologist who studied as a disciple of Ernst Leumann (~1904–1906). He later held an appointment as a professor at the University of Hamburg (attested 1958).

Walther Wüst (1901–1993) worked in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1919–1923), where he later served as rector from 1941 to 1946.
